investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or readiness steps required by the expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining VM slots (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Preemption was also unavailable on both node groups. Because the pod remained unscheduled for ~146 s, the eval runner timed out before createAgent() could return an agentId or vmId, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the contract validation to fail. This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or readiness steps required by the expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining VM slots (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Preemption was also unavailable on both node groups. Because the pod remained unscheduled for ~146 s, the eval runner timed out before createAgent() could return an agentId or vmId, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the contract validation to fail. This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

Because the agent pod never scheduled, the eval probe never reached the agent runtime, and zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were returned, causing a complete contract gap.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes do not match the affinity/selector at all. With no schedulable node and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck Unschedulable for ~144–147 seconds before the probe timed out. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. This is an eval-detected infrastructure failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a simultaneous user-facing outage, though the same scheduling constraint would affect real remote-agent provisioning requests.
